source.section: PDF page 7 'Examples of Income You DO NOT Report' (Defined Benefit Retirement Plan, IRC 414(j)); PDF page 14 Pensions and Annuities (401(k)(2) on Schedule RS); Form 40 page 2 Part I line 4; Form 40 (25f40blk.pdf page 1) lines 5b to 18; booklet PDF page 8 lines 5 to 13, PDF page 10 lines 14 and 17; PDF page 9 Standard Deduction chart (line 11, PDF page 8); Form 40 page 1 boxes 1 to 4 (personal exemption, line 13); tax table PDF pages 25 to 30

worked: Federal AGI = private defined benefit pension 30,000.00 + 401(k) distribution (person 0) 25,000.00 = 55,000.00. Federal taxable income = 55,000.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction = 39,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Alabama: the projection starts from federal AGI and removes exempt income (Form 40 builds its own lines 5b to 10, which give the same AGI for this household). Subtract private defined benefit pension 30,000.00: payments from a 'Defined Benefit Retirement Plan' in accordance with IRC 414(j) are not reported (PDF page 7; PDF page 14); the projection treats every private pension as such a plan (approximation). 401(k) distribution 25,000.00 stays in: 401(k)(2) distributions are reported and taxed on Schedule RS, Form 40 page 2 Part I line 4 (PDF page 14 'use these lines to report distributions from SEP, Keogh, 401(k)(2), 403(b), and profit sharing plans'); the defined benefit relief does not cover employer_plan_distribution. Form 40 line 10 Alabama AGI = 25,000.00. Line 11 standard deduction (single, chart PDF page 9): AL AGI 25,000.00 is in the first band (0 to 25,999.00), the full amount, so 3,000.00. Line 12 federal income tax deduction: the form subtracts the 2025 federal income tax (worksheet PDF page 31); the projection does not model it (not_modelled, approximation), so 0.00 here. Line 13 personal exemption (single) 1,500.00. Line 14 dependent exemption 0.00 (no dependents). Line 15 total deductions = 3,000.00 + 0.00 + 1,500.00 + 0.00 = 4,500.00. Line 16 taxable income = 25,000.00 - 4,500.00 = 20,500.00. Line 17 tax from the derived single / married filing separately / head of family schedule (2% from 0, 4% from 500, 5% from 3,000): (500.00 - 0.00) x 0.02 = 10.00 + (3,000.00 - 500.00) x 0.04 = 100.00 + (20,500.00 - 3,000.00) x 0.05 = 875.00 = 985.00; the tax table row 20,500-20,600 (single / married filing separately / head of family column, PDF pages 25 to 30) gives 988. Line 18 net tax due, no credits: 985.00.
accepted_approximations: The federal income tax deduction is not applied (not_modelled).

The brackets are derived from the tax table. Under 100,000 the table taxes each 100-dollar row at its midpoint, rounded; above 100,000 the printed worksheet ((income - 100,000) x .05 + 4,958, or + 4,918 joint) is 2 dollars below the derived brackets.

Every private pension and every other state's government pension is treated as paid by a plan that qualifies as a defined benefit plan under IRC 414(j), and every Alabama or federal government pension as exempt; the booklet exempts only the listed systems and qualifying 414(j) plans and leaves qualification to the plan administrator.
